description.en: Two neighbouring kingdoms of the southern Levant: Israel in the north, with its capital at Samaria, and Judah in the south, around Jerusalem. Assyria ended Israel around 722 BCE and Babylon ended Judah in 587 or 586 BCE. The Bible's account and the archaeology differ on their early years.
description.es: Dos reinos vecinos del Levante meridional: Israel al norte, con capital en Samaria, y Judá al sur, en torno a Jerusalén. Asiria puso fin a Israel hacia 722 a. e. c. y Babilonia a Judá en 587 o 586 a. e. c. El relato bíblico y la arqueología difieren sobre sus primeros años.
description.zh: 黎凡特南部相邻的两个王国：北方的以色列，都城撒玛利亚；南方的犹大，以耶路撒冷为中心。亚述约在公元前722年灭亡以色列，巴比伦于公元前587或586年灭亡犹大。《圣经》的叙述与考古发现在其早期历史上并不一致。

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Israel" (northern kingdom destroyed by the Assyrians in 722 BCE; split after Solomon's death).
Livius.org, "Samaria" (Solomon's kingdom divided after his death c. 931; Omri, 884–873, founded Samaria; Israel became an Assyrian province c. 724).
Livius.org, "Jerusalem" (siege by Sennacherib in 701 bought off; city captured by Nebuchadnezzar in 587).

note.en: The Bible dates the two kingdoms from a split c. 930 BCE after a united kingdom under David and Solomon. Archaeologists disagree on whether that united state existed: Israel Finkelstein's low chronology moves the 10th-century monumental buildings into the 9th century, while William Dever and others read the 10th-century evidence as consistent with one. Israel is firmly attested by Assyrian records from the 9th century BCE, and many archaeologists place Judah's rise as a substantial state in the 8th century BCE.
note.es: La Biblia fecha los dos reinos a partir de una división hacia 930 a. e. c., tras un reino unido bajo David y Salomón. Los arqueólogos discrepan sobre si ese estado unido existió: la cronología baja de Israel Finkelstein traslada al siglo IX los edificios monumentales del siglo X, mientras que William Dever y otros consideran que las pruebas del siglo X son compatibles con él. Israel está bien atestiguado por registros asirios desde el siglo IX a. e. c., y muchos arqueólogos sitúan el auge de Judá como estado importante en el siglo VIII a. e. c.
note.zh: 《圣经》认为，在大卫和所罗门治下的统一王国之后，两个王国于约公元前930年分裂。考古学家对这个统一国家是否存在意见不一：以色列·芬克尔斯坦的“低年代学”把10世纪的宏伟建筑移到9世纪，而威廉·德弗等人认为10世纪的证据与统一国家相符。以色列自公元前9世纪起就有亚述记录确证，许多考古学家认为犹大到公元前8世纪才成为较大的国家。

sources.citation: International Congress on Biblical Archaeology (1985). Biblical Archaeology Today, via PeriodO: "Israelite Age" (1200 – 586 BCE).

name.en: Israel and Judah side by side
name.es: Israel y Judá, lado a lado

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Israel" (northern kingdom destroyed by the Assyrians in 722 BCE; split after Solomon's death).
Livius.org, "Samaria" (Solomon's kingdom divided after his death c. 931; Omri, 884–873, founded Samaria; Israel became an Assyrian province c. 724).
Livius.org, "Jerusalem" (siege by Sennacherib in 701 bought off; city captured by Nebuchadnezzar in 587).
World History Encyclopedia, "Nebuchadnezzar II" (destruction of Jerusalem in 587/586 BCE).

title.en: Pharaoh Merneptah's victory stele names a people called Israel in Canaan, the earliest known mention
title.es: La estela de victoria del faraón Merenptah nombra a un pueblo llamado Israel en Canaán, la mención más antigua conocida
title.zh: 法老美楞普塔的胜利碑文提到迦南有一个名为以色列的民族，这是已知最早的记载

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, Jacob Wright (Emory University), "The Oldest Reference to Israel" (stele dating to 1208 BCE, found by Petrie in 1896).
Egypt Museum, "Victory Stele of Merneptah" (Egyptian Museum, Cairo, JE 31408; the name Israel in line 27 refers to a people; found by Petrie in 1896).
Wikipedia, "Merneptah Stele" (c. 1208 BCE; Egyptian Museum, Cairo).

note.en: The sign after the name marks a people, not a city or state, and most scholars place this Israel among the people of Canaan's hill country. It is about 350 years before Israel's king Ahab appears in Assyrian records (853 BCE).
note.es: El signo tras el nombre indica un pueblo, no una ciudad ni un estado, y la mayoría de los especialistas sitúan a este Israel entre la población de la región montañosa de Canaán. Es unos 350 años anterior a la aparición del rey Acab de Israel en los registros asirios (853 a. e. c.).
note.zh: 名字后的限定符表示这是一个民族，而非城市或国家，多数学者认为这个以色列属于迦南山地的居民。它比以色列国王亚哈出现在亚述记录中（公元前853年）早约350年。

title.en: In the Bible's account, the kingdom of David and Solomon splits into Israel in the north and Judah in the south
title.es: Según el relato bíblico, el reino de David y Salomón se divide en Israel, al norte, y Judá, al sur
title.zh: 据《圣经》记载，大卫和所罗门的王国分裂为北方的以色列与南方的犹大

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Israel" (northern kingdom destroyed by the Assyrians in 722 BCE; split after Solomon's death).
Livius.org, "Samaria" (Solomon's kingdom divided after his death c. 931; Omri, 884–873, founded Samaria; Israel became an Assyrian province c. 724).

note.en: Whether one kingdom existed before the split is debated. The earliest mention outside the Bible of a 'House of David' is the Tel Dan stele, from the 9th century BCE.
note.es: Se discute si existió un solo reino antes de la división. La mención más antigua fuera de la Biblia de una 'Casa de David' es la estela de Tel Dan, del siglo IX a. e. c.
note.zh: 分裂之前是否存在一个统一王国尚有争论。《圣经》之外最早提到“大卫之家”的是公元前9世纪的特尔但碑。

title.en: Omri makes Samaria the capital of Israel; Assyrian records call the kingdom the House of Omri
title.es: Omrí convierte Samaria en capital de Israel; los registros asirios llaman al reino la Casa de Omrí
title.zh: 暗利定撒玛利亚为以色列都城；亚述记录称这个王国为“暗利之家”

sources.citation: Livius.org, "Samaria" (Omri, 884–873, founded Samaria in the sixth year of his reign).
Wikipedia, "Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)" (capital moved from Tirzah to Samaria around 880 BCE).

note.en: Omri's reign is dated 884–873 BCE by Livius and about 876–869 BCE by other chronologies, so founding Samaria in his sixth year falls between about 879 and 871 BCE. The year here is a middle estimate.
note.es: Livius fecha el reinado de Omrí en 884–873 a. e. c. y otras cronologías en c. 876–869 a. e. c., de modo que la fundación de Samaria, en su sexto año, cae entre c. 879 y 871 a. e. c. El año indicado es una estimación intermedia.
note.zh: Livius将暗利在位定为公元前884至873年，其他年表则为约公元前876至869年，因此他在位第六年建立撒玛利亚，约在公元前879至871年之间。此处的年份是折中的估计。

title.en: Ahab of Israel joins a coalition against Shalmaneser III of Assyria at Qarqar; only Assyrian records mention it
title.es: Acab de Israel se une a una coalición contra Salmanasar III de Asiria en Qarqar; solo los registros asirios la mencionan
title.zh: 以色列的亚哈在卡尔卡尔加入对抗亚述沙勒马内色三世的联军；只有亚述记录提到这场战役

sources.citation: Encyclopaedia Judaica, "Karkar" (via Encyclopedia.com): battle in Shalmaneser III's sixth year, 853 BCE; Ahab the Israelite listed with 2,000 chariots and 10,000 foot soldiers; the Bible does not mention it.
World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Israel" (Assyrian records give Ahab 2,000 chariots and 10,000 infantry; modern scholarship contests the numbers).
Wikipedia, "Battle of Qarqar" (853 BC; Kurkh Monolith).

note.en: The Kurkh Monolith credits Ahab with 2,000 chariots and 10,000 soldiers; some scholars think the chariot figure is too high. The date, 853 BCE, comes from Shalmaneser III's sixth regnal year. The Hebrew Bible does not mention the battle.
note.es: El Monolito de Kurkh atribuye a Acab 2000 carros y 10 000 soldados; algunos especialistas consideran excesiva la cifra de carros. La fecha, 853 a. e. c., procede del sexto año de reinado de Salmanasar III. La Biblia hebrea no menciona la batalla.
note.zh: 库尔赫巨石碑称亚哈出动2000辆战车和1万名士兵；一些学者认为战车数字偏高。公元前853年这一年代来自沙勒马内色三世在位第六年。《希伯来圣经》没有提到这场战役。

title.en: Assyria takes Samaria and ends the kingdom of Israel; many of its people are deported
title.es: Asiria toma Samaria y pone fin al reino de Israel; muchos de sus habitantes son deportados
title.zh: 亚述攻占撒玛利亚，灭亡以色列王国，许多居民被迁走

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Kingdom of Israel" (northern kingdom destroyed by the Assyrians in 722 BCE; split after Solomon's death).
Livius.org, "Samaria" (Solomon's kingdom divided after his death c. 931; Omri, 884–873, founded Samaria; Israel became an Assyrian province c. 724).
Wikipedia, "Kingdom of Israel (Samaria)" (conquered around 720 BCE; Sargon II's record of carrying off 27,280 people).

note.en: Sources date the fall between about 724 and 720 BCE (Livius c. 724, the World History Encyclopedia 722, Wikipedia c. 720). Scholars estimate that far fewer people were resettled than Assyrian records claim.
note.es: Las fuentes datan la caída entre c. 724 y 720 a. e. c. (Livius c. 724, la World History Encyclopedia 722, Wikipedia c. 720). Los especialistas calculan que se reasentó a muchas menos personas de las que afirman los registros asirios.
note.zh: 各资料将陷落定在约公元前724年至前720年之间（Livius约前724年，《世界历史百科全书》前722年，维基百科约前720年）。学者估计，实际迁走的人数远少于亚述记录所称。

title.en: Sennacherib of Assyria takes Lachish and besieges Jerusalem under Hezekiah, but does not take the city
title.es: Senaquerib de Asiria toma Laquis y asedia Jerusalén bajo Ezequías, pero no conquista la ciudad
title.zh: 亚述的西拿基立攻占拉吉，并围攻希西家治下的耶路撒冷，但未能攻下该城

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Sennacherib" (701 BCE campaign; Lachish besieged and taken while envoys demanded Jerusalem's surrender).
Livius.org, "Jerusalem" (siege by Sennacherib in 701 bought off; city captured by Nebuchadnezzar in 587).

title.en: Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon destroys Jerusalem and its Temple, ending the kingdom of Judah
title.es: Nabucodonosor II de Babilonia destruye Jerusalén y su Templo, y pone fin al reino de Judá
title.zh: 巴比伦的尼布甲尼撒二世毁灭耶路撒冷及其圣殿，犹大王国灭亡

sources.citation: World History Encyclopedia, "Nebuchadnezzar II" (destruction of Jerusalem in 587/586 BCE).
Livius.org, "Jerusalem" (siege by Sennacherib in 701 bought off; city captured by Nebuchadnezzar in 587).
Wikipedia, "Siege of Jerusalem (587 BC)" (burn layer; 587 versus 586 BC).

note.en: Historians put the fall of Jerusalem in 587 or 586 BCE, depending on how they count the years of King Zedekiah's reign.
note.es: Los historiadores sitúan la caída de Jerusalén en 587 o 586 a. e. c., según cómo cuenten los años del reinado de Sedecías.
note.zh: 历史学家将耶路撒冷陷落定在公元前587年或586年，取决于如何计算西底家在位的年数。

text.en: Hezekiah's Tunnel under Jerusalem is about 533 metres long; its inscription says two teams dug from opposite ends and met in the middle. It is traditionally dated to about 700 BCE, but a 2011 study argues for the late 9th or early 8th century.
text.es: El túnel de Ezequías bajo Jerusalén mide unos 533 metros; su inscripción dice que dos equipos excavaron desde extremos opuestos y se encontraron en el centro. Tradicionalmente se fecha hacia 700 a. e. c., pero un estudio de 2011 propone finales del siglo IX o principios del VIII.
text.zh: 耶路撒冷地下的希西家水道长约533米；其铭文称两队人马从两端相向开凿，在中间会合。传统上定在约公元前700年，但2011年的一项研究认为应在公元前9世纪末或8世纪初。

sources.citation: Livius.org, "The Siloam Inscription" (533 m tunnel to the Siloam pool; inscription now in the Istanbul Archaeological Museum).
Wikipedia, "Hezekiah's Tunnel" (533 m; traditionally c. 700 BCE; 2011 excavations suggest the late 9th or early 8th century BCE).
